title: A controlled-substance prescription may be refilled only if the original provides for refills and states their number
rule_summary: Under M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 23(f), no prescription for a controlled substance shall be refilled unless the original prescription provides for such refilling and unless the number of refills has been specified in said prescription. Section 1 of chapter 94C defines a controlled substance as a drug, substance, controlled substance analogue or immediate precursor in any schedule or class referred to in the chapter, and s. 2(a) establishes, besides five schedules incorporating the federal schedules, a sixth schedule which shall include all prescription drugs not included in the first five. The refill condition in s. 23(f) therefore reaches a Schedule VI prescription as well as a prescription in Schedules III through V.
exam_relevance: Tests that in Massachusetts a refill needs the original prescription to provide for refilling and to state the number of refills, for Schedule VI as for Schedules III through V.

authority.name: Massachusetts General Laws
authority.section: M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 1, definition of Controlled substance

common_confusions: Treating an original prescription that is silent on refills as refillable.
Assuming the refill condition reaches only federally scheduled drugs, when chapter 94C's definition of a controlled substance includes a drug in Schedule VI.
verification_notes: M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 23(f), the definition of controlled substance in s. 1, and s. 2(a) read in the current text on malegislature.gov on 2026-09-11. Added as a new rule so that no released adjudication is disturbed.
